The rumored foldable iPhone Ultra is set to launch within weeks. As we've previously written, anticipation for this device is building.

Bloomberg published a new report today featuring impressions from Apple employees who have tried the iPhone Ultra.

iPhone Ultra incoming: real-world usage impressions

In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman rounded up details about the foldable iPhone. He specifically noted that he had spoken with "several people" who have used the device. These people said they particularly liked the following:

  • The device fits comfortably in a pants pocket. The rumored cover display is 5.5 inches.
  • The hinge durability.
  • A new "iPad-like app layout" that makes use of the inner display space. The inner display is reportedly around 7.8 inches and wider in aspect ratio.
  • The performance when used as a "viewfinder".

Multiple reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will be priced above $2,000. It's expected to feature main and ultrawide cameras but no telephoto lens. Touch ID is reportedly set to replace Face ID for biometrics.

9to5Mac's take

I'm very excited about the iPhone Ultra, and the details Gurman shared make me even more optimistic that it'll be the right fit for me.

I had reservations about the foldable iPhone's design, but as we've learned more about its specific dimensions and benefits, I've come around.

The positive reception of Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 also provides valuable real-world reference for a design that's expected to be very similar to the iPhone Ultra.

Of course, there will be trade-offs compared to the iPhone 18 Pro. I'm currently using an iPhone Air, so I'm already accustomed to life without a telephoto lens, and going back to Touch ID wouldn't be a major change.

What do you think of the iPhone Ultra rumors? Will you be picking one up this fall? Share your thoughts in the comments section.
